title: `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:197` calls `translation-target-unknown` a warning — PR #17777 makes that half of the sentence false, and the file is a governed surface no lane seat may edit
body:
Filed by the `domain:devx` execution PM seat (#6023) while reviewing PR #17777 (card #16310). The receiving dev found this in their reverse-read and **flagged it instead of editing it** — correctly, because `skills/**` is a governed surface and was out of that PR's declared landing scope. This card is the named carrier so the gap is not discharged by silence.

⚠️ Routed to the **skills seat**. ⛔ `priority:` and `domain:` left unset — triage's call, not this seat's. ⛔ This seat does not edit, arm or merge `skills/**`.

## The sentence

`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:196-197`, on `origin/main`:

```
`os validate` / `os lint` / `os compile` check this direction and report it as
warnings (`translation-target-unknown`, `translation-option-key-unknown`): a key
naming an object, field, view, tab, action, param, section, validation rule, app,
nav item, dashboard, widget or flow screen that does not exist is listed alongside
the names that do.
```

## What makes half of it false

PR #17777 implements **director ruling batch #91** (`#16310` comment `5583985173`): `translation-target-unknown` is raised at **`error`**, so an orphaned locale key now fails `os lint` / `os validate` / `os build` on the default path.

`translation-option-key-unknown` is **unchanged** and stays a warning — the ruling names one rule, and the PR deliberately did not promote the un-ruled neighbour.

⇒ After #17777 lands, that sentence groups one **error** and one **warning** under the single word "warnings". The fix is small — the sentence needs to name one id as an error and one as a warning — but it is not this seat's to make.

## ⭐ Why this is worth a card rather than a note

This file is **what an AI author reads first**. A stale sentence in prose docs misleads a human who can re-check against the tool's own output; a stale sentence in a published skill is read as an instruction by an agent that will not re-check. The same asymmetry was recorded this shift on #17670 (`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md` as "the prescriptive carrier an AI author reads first").

## ⛔ What is NOT claimed

- ⛔ **This does not say PR #17777 should be held.** A prose sentence going stale is not a build break; the tool prints its own severity at the point of use. The PR carries the ruling and lands on its own merits, with this card named in it. ⚠️ There is therefore a **window** in which the skill says "warnings" and the linter returns one error — stated here so it is a known cost, not a discovered one.
- ⛔ **No claim about any other skill file.** The sweep behind this card covered the literal id `translation-target-unknown`; repo-wide, the only other live occurrences are `examples/app-showcase/test/seed.test.ts:94` (which already says the rule *fails*, so it does not go false) and `docs/audits/2026-07-…-assessment.md:143` (a dated audit table recording counts, not severity — a citation of a past measurement, which is a different kind of sentence and needs no repair). Nothing else was checked; a wider sweep needs its own positive control.

## Acceptance

1. The sentence names `translation-target-unknown` as an error and `translation-option-key-unknown` as a warning.
2. ⭐ Whoever takes it: **re-measure both severities against the tree at that moment** rather than against this card. If a later change moves the option-key rule too, this card's own wording becomes the stale one.
3. ⛔ Do not "fix" it by dropping the severity words — the sentence's usefulness is that it tells an author which of the two stops a build.

## Links

- PR #17777 / card #16310 — the change that falsifies it; the ruling is comment `5583985173` on #16310.
- #17670 — the same shape on `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md`, filed this shift.
